actual_checks: Full exact prompt, source/meta wrappers, report, source notes and author/contribution records read. Official metadata lists no priors. The scope is a significant exact conditional route to exponent one, with the full Korselt criterion and analytic hypothesis boundaries, correctly labeled literature report rather than unconditional resolution.

Heath-Brown least-prime hypothesis has uniform constants in residue and modulus, of form P(a,m)<=K*m*(log m)^A. Source theorem loss (2+o(1))*loglogloglog X/logloglog X tends to zero; trivial upper count bound squeezes the logarithmic exponent to one. Strict versus nonstrict cutoffs differ at most one, negligible because the lower count grows at least a positive power eventually.

Checked every step of Korselt proof: CRT unit 1+p modulo p^2 disproves repeated prime factors via n-1=-1 mod p; lifted primitive generators force p-1|n-1. Converse uses square-freeness and CRT. The all-integer a^n=a version follows prime-by-prime. Products of at least two distinct primes p=dk+1 with d|L and n=1 mod kL meet the criterion.

A fixed Linnik power m^L, L>1, does not imply an almost-linear logarithmic-power bound; no GRH-to-hypothesis implication is asserted. The report separates exponent-one counting from positive density and keeps dated introductory bounds distinct from a current-best survey.
